central_tensions: Decorrelation vs. correlated draws: the entire value of a 'fleet' over a single strong review rests on the claim (C-033) that commit-and-reveal plus opposed objective functions make a same-model fleet 'more than N correlated draws' — but every seat and every verifier is the same Claude model sharing the same priors and blind spots. Does the architecture genuinely decorrelate, or does it relaunder one model's judgment with extra steps?

Absolute guarantees vs. probabilistic reality: the design asserts hard invariants — 'Invented numbers are structurally impossible' (C-040, C-060), 'impeccable revised paper' (C-005), 'No fabricated citations, numbers, quotes, data, or results — ever' (C-018). Yet the Runner/Scribe wall, the quote-gate, and the panel are all enforced by prompts and one substring script. Are these enforced invariants or aspirational rules the model can still violate (e.g., a Runner producing a hash-stamped number from wrong/misread code)?

Exhaustiveness claims vs. what is actually checked: 'every argument, every word' (C-003), 'covered == total' (C-022, C-055), and 'better than any conference' (C-016) are presented as checked invariants. But a per-range verdict proves a range was visited, not that its argument was meaningfully reviewed; is the coverage certificate substantive assurance or coverage theater at scale?

Act II safety vs. error-laundering: re-running the author's code and auto-implementing presentation/additive edits, gated only by Claude verifiers plus author sign-off, is the differentiator (C-027). Does the Execution-Provenance Wall plus author ratification actually protect the scientific record, or can it lend a veneer of provenance to a mis-specified or non-reproducing pipeline?
